**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Note this is a `feat`: per AGENTS.md it merges at the next minor cut, not between cuts.

## What looks good

- The reach law reuses `verify::solid_hits` through its public seam (`Cutter`, `SolidLaw`) - no copied geometry, and the probe gets the same swept-solid judgement the cutters get. The stack in `stylus_cutter` matches how `Cutter::atoms()` partitions: the lower-hemisphere Bull atom is the edge (a ball penetration is still the ball law's `Gouge`), and the stem band starting at `flute_len` is body, so a stem-only meeting reads `ShankHit { part: true }` - refused by name, as the issue asked.
- Conservative in the safe direction: stem at the ball radius, body at `max(shank, holder)` radius over the combined length - never smaller than the real stack, so it can over-report but cannot miss a meeting (documented honestly in the readings and the decision file).
- Dedup by move index is right: a move the ball law convicted isn't reported twice, and a ball the distance law misses (wholly inside the solid) is kept as the solid law's `Gouge`. Degenerate tools fail closed (`atoms()` guards non-finite/non-positive geometry, `solid_hits` returns a `Gouge` at the first cutting move) - never a silent pass.
- No new `Warning` variant - correctly reasoned: `Warning` is a cached-path file format, and `ShankHit`'s text already reads "shank/holder ... collides" everywhere it is named. No project-format or output-format change.
- Tangency is handled by the existing `STYLUS_SLACK` allowance, and the clean fixtures prove it: edge/face/corner touches on all sides stay warning-free under the combined law.
- `probe_op.rs` (157 lines) and `probe_reach.rs` (201 lines) stay well inside the 400-line law; both carry provenance and the suite carries a gate map. The decision file follows the `docs/decisions/<issue>-<slug>.md` format. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests, no UI-state writes (so no new command needed), no `CHANGELOG.md` edit.

## Local results, merged with main

Trial merge with current `main` (`bd37a3b`) was clean - no conflicts; main has not touched `probe_op`, `verify`, `probing` or `tools` since this PR's base. Windows x64, debug:

| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` | build ok |
| `probe_reach` (new suite) | 5 passed, 0 failed |
| `probe_op` (existing suite) | 11 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-app --lib` | 92 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

## Requested before merge

Nothing.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The solid law judges the assembly against the mesh's point-in-solid parity; for a non-watertight model mesh the verdict is only as honest as the shell (the index fails closed only on non-finite vertices). This is pre-existing solid-law behaviour, not something this PR introduces - but since the probe op now goes through it for the first time, an open-shell model will now convict probe moves that previously read clean by the ball-only law. That is the safe direction (a meeting is refused, never passed), so no change asked - just flagging it for the changelog entry's wording.
- `probe_cycle` emits only straight moves, so the `SolidLaw.step` sampling (vertical-plane arcs) costs nothing here - a nice fit, worth knowing if arcs ever enter probe paths later.
- Commit scope `feat(sim)` reads fine: the judgement comes from sim's solid law; the code lands in app's probe op. No action.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
